findings.title: Leaderboard operation matrix contradicts the accepted unchanged-public contract

sourceEvidence.explanation: The supplied baseline currently requires a session and institute input. The revised architecture explicitly says the public leaderboard must remain anonymous and unchanged under U-01, but the assigned operation-matrix row instead defines COURSE_READ authentication, normal-role tenant authorization, and SUPER_USER denial. Those are mutually incompatible target contracts.

The existing response is an institute leaderboard. The design must decide how its public institute selection and privacy behavior are preserved; the assigned row instead treats the operation as a protected course read.

findings.impact: Implementers and reviewers cannot determine whether GET must remain anonymously accessible or become authenticated. Implementing the matrix would violate the accepted U-01 decision, while following the narrative would make the assigned matrix row, denial expectations, and future case definition incorrect. This blocks trustworthy implementation and verification for this operation.
findings.recommendation: Revise the assigned operation-matrix row to PUBLIC with the existing anonymous leaderboard semantics, remove actor-role and SUPER_USER-specific denial requirements, and bind its future case to public institute selection plus existing privacy controls. Keep the route review-only and non-modification-eligible as the revised narrative requires.

findings.title: Tag creation matrix grants a broader role set than the preserved operation contract

sourceEvidence.explanation: The supplied source establishes the existing operation-specific contract: only instructor or administrator roles may create tags; other eligible ICS users receive 403.

After the instructor/Admin check, the handler performs existence reads and creates the global tag. The assigned POST matrix row uses the generic KX role set including STUDENT and contains no operation-specific instructor/Admin relation.

findings.impact: The revised design simultaneously promises preservation of legitimate existing domain behavior and assigns POST tag creation to a generic KX policy whose normalRoles include STUDENT. An implementation following that row could authorize students to mutate the shared tag taxonomy, and future verification derived from the row would encode that privilege expansion.
findings.recommendation: Give POST /knowledge-exchange/tags an explicit creation rule limited to canonical instructor aliases and ADMIN, with actual active ICS institute binding and SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial before body parsing or database access. Preserve GET under the broader eligible KX read contract. Update the POST matrix row and its unique verification case accordingly.

implementationRisks.title: Current role normalization maps unknown and SUPER_USER values to STUDENT

sourceEvidence.explanation: Every role other than ADMIN or an instructor alias falls through to STUDENT.
KX routes consume normalizeRole and return that result without an explicit recognized-role or SUPER_USER rejection.

implementationRisks.impact: Until implemented, KX routes can interpret SUPER_USER or malformed role values as STUDENT, contrary to the revised UNKNOWN fail-closed and hard legacy ceiling contract.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Implement a canonical role resolver with explicit SUPER_USER and UNKNOWN results, then require an allowed normal role at every assigned protected entry before parsing inputs, protected reads, writes, or side effects.

implementationRisks.title: KX search and voting do not enforce persisted parent visibility and course relationships

sourceEvidence.explanation: Search constrains posts to non-deleted ICS records but does not constrain course-linked posts by the actor's approved enrollment, instructor assignment, or Admin authority.

Vote target lookup reads only authorId, voteCount, and deletion state; answers are not resolved through their parent post, and neither target is checked for institute, course visibility, enrollment, or assignment.
Vote mutations and author EXP effects execute after the incomplete target checks.

implementationRisks.impact: Before implementation, recognized ICS actors may search or vote on course-linked content without the required persisted course relationship, and unauthorized mutations can trigger vote-count and gamification effects.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Resolve each post, and each answer through its parent post, with institute/status/deletion and course membership predicates before returning content or entering the mutation transaction. Keep vote ownership bound to the canonical actor and perform EXP only after the authorized committed vote result.

implementationRisks.title: Material annotation operations lack student-role, enrollment, institute, and material-parent authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: GET checks only for a session and filters annotations by attachmentId and userId; it does not resolve Attachment to SyllabusItem and Course or validate STUDENT role and APPROVED enrollment.
POST accepts an attachmentId and creates an annotation for the session user without resolving or authorizing the attachment's actual material, course, institute, or enrollment.
DELETE verifies annotation ownership but does not resolve its attachment and course boundary or require the MATERIAL policy's student enrollment relationship.

implementationRisks.impact: Until implemented, authenticated non-students and students without access to the underlying course material can reach annotation reads or writes, and SUPER_USER is not explicitly denied before protected processing.
implementationRisks.recommendation: At each method entry enforce canonical STUDENT role, then resolve annotation/attachment through SyllabusItem and Course with matching actor institute and APPROVED enrollment. Use uniform safe 404 for foreign or inaccessible parents and deny SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before parsing protected identifiers.

implementationRisks.title: Material completion grants gamification effects without MATERIAL authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: The handler obtains a generic workspace session, parses a caller-selected syllabus item ID, and reads the item without checking STUDENT role, MATERIAL type, course institute, or APPROVED enrollment.
The handler grants EXP and evaluates a badge using the unverified item and caller-supplied duration.

implementationRisks.impact: Any authenticated session, including SUPER_USER or a user unrelated to the course, may trigger material EXP and badge effects for an arbitrary syllabus item until the design is implemented.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Deny SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN and non-STUDENT actors before parsing; resolve an actual MATERIAL syllabus item through its course, actor institute, and APPROVED enrollment before any completion, EXP, badge, notification, or study effect.

implementationRisks.title: Own-notification and avatar routes do not enforce the Super User legacy ceiling

sourceEvidence.explanation: Any authenticated session reaches request parsing and a success response; no allowed-role or SUPER_USER denial exists.
Both methods authorize solely by the presence of a session and operate on that session user's notifications, without excluding SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN.
Both methods allow any authenticated session to create or delete an in-memory subscription, with no role ceiling.
Any authenticated session can parse avatar input and update its User record; the revised contract permits SUPER_USER only login, logout, and /api/auth/me.

implementationRisks.impact: Until implemented, SUPER_USER can access notification, subscription, push-token, and profile-management operations expressly excluded by the revised basic-support contract. Unknown role values are also not rejected.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Apply the canonical resolver at each entry, allow only the OWN policy's recognized normal roles, and return 403 for SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before request-body parsing, protected reads, registry changes, or User/Notification mutations.

implementationRisks.title: Push-token registration is only an echo and subscription state is process-local

sourceEvidence.explanation: The handler echoes the submitted token and deviceType without validation, ownership-bound persistence, or an actual registration effect.
Subscription state is held in a module-local Map.
A single value keyed only by user ID is written or removed, so state is not durable across processes and DELETE cannot select a particular owned device subscription.

implementationRisks.impact: Even after role denial is added, the current endpoints cannot reliably provide durable, multi-device, ownership-bound notification registration semantics in a distributed deployment.
implementationRisks.recommendation: During implementation, define the actual owned subscription/token persistence contract, validate endpoint/token/device data, bind records to actor and device identity, and make deletion target only an owned record. If these endpoints are intentionally placeholders, document and verify their no-registration semantics rather than returning misleading success.

coverage.assessment: Reviewed GET as KX. The revised target requires a canonical recognized normal-role actor, actual ICS institute, persisted visibility/course relationship, and SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial before protected input and reads. Current missing relationship enforcement is recorded as an implementation risk.

Reviewed both assigned methods. GET is a KX tag read for recognized ICS normal roles. POST has an unresolved design defect because the generic matrix role set includes STUDENT while the preserved source contract restricts creation to instructor/Admin.

Reviewed POST as an actor-owned KX mutation requiring resolution of post or answer through the actual parent post, institute, visibility, and any linked-course relationship before vote and EXP effects. Baseline gaps remain unimplemented.

Reviewed GET against accepted U-01 public behavior. The narrative says anonymous and unchanged, but the assigned matrix specifies authenticated COURSE_READ and SUPER_USER denial; this HIGH contract contradiction prevents readiness.

Reviewed all three MATERIAL operations. Each must require canonical STUDENT role, actual attachment-to-item-to-course resolution, matching institute, APPROVED enrollment, actor-owned annotation where applicable, and early SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial.

Reviewed POST as MATERIAL/STUDENT_WORK-like completion with gamification effects. Authorization must precede protected parsing/read and bind the material to an actual same-institute approved enrollment; baseline exposure is not remediated.

Reviewed POST under OWN for normal roles and the explicit Super User support ceiling. SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN must receive 403 before body parsing or registration effects; the existing echo-only behavior is separately recorded as an implementation risk.

Reviewed GET and PATCH under OWN. Notification selection/mutation is actor-ID scoped in the baseline, but the revised design additionally requires canonical normal-role recognition and early SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial.
Reviewed both OWN subscription methods. The revised support ceiling requires early SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial; durable and device-specific ownership semantics remain an implementation concern.

Reviewed PUT under OWN for normal roles. Because profile support is excluded for SUPER_USER, the route must reject SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN before body parsing and User mutation while preserving normal-role self-only behavior.

limitations: Review was limited exactly to the ten assigned route paths, fifteen assigned HTTP methods, the supplied revised architecture, assigned matrix rows, and necessary shared policy/source excerpts.
No tools, filesystem access, commands, network requests, tests, database operations, source changes, approvals, or other reviewer outputs were used, as required.

The packet supplies no explicit comprehensive acceptance-criteria catalog beyond named identifiers such as U-01 and META-01; affectedAC therefore uses the applicable supplied U-01 identifier and does not invent additional AC IDs.
No implementation, runtime behavior, passing test, transaction execution, formal gate, lease, or product validation is claimed. All implementation risks remain NOT_REMEDIATED and unresolved.

Operational META-01 approver, maintainer, production dataset/fingerprint, expiry lifetime, and publication/runbook identities remain required human/operator assignments in the wider design. They do not directly govern these assigned legacy routes, and none were invented here.
